title: Pipirima: Predicting Patterns in Sparsity to Accelerate Matrix Algebra
problem: Sparse accelerators struggle with load imbalance when processing compressed sparse matrices due to unpredictable non-zero value distributions, limiting performance despite sparsity optimization opportunities.
motivation: Sparsity in scientific computing and transformers offers significant acceleration potential, but load imbalance and unpredictability remain bottlenecks in accelerator design.
method: Pipirima predicts where non-zero values will appear in sparse matrices using simple counters inspired by CPU branch predictors. When streaming through a compressed matrix (CSR, a compact way to store sparse matrices), these predictions let the accelerator prepare its processing units in advance, preventing load imbalance where some units sit idle while others are overloaded. The system is tested on sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) and sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpMM).
key_novelty: Pipirima uses simple counters to predict where non-zero values appear in sparse matrices, which helps accelerators distribute work evenly across their processors.
contributions: 6x speedup over Tensaurus for SpMM; 4x for SpMV on SuiteSparse
8.3x and 48.2x speedup vs Tensaurus and ExTensor on sparse transformer workloads
5.621 mm^2 area and 544.93 mW power at 45nm technology
Minimal area/power overhead for prediction logic
limitations: Evaluation limited to CSR format; applicability to other sparse formats and dynamic sparsity patterns unclear.
primary_theme: Pattern prediction for sparse matrix acceleration
